text:
Mia: Heads up — noticed a spike in p95/p99 on /v1/generate (redwood-medium, us-west-2) starting ~2026-03-15T19:10Z. p95 jumped from ~400ms to ~1.6s, p99 to ~3.2s. A few upstream 502s reported by customers. Grafana: https://grafana.internal/r/xyz (latency dashboard)
Alex: On it. Any obvious errors in inference logs? Are we seeing CUDA OOMs or just timeouts?
Mia: Logs show repeated allocation fallbacks and long tails. Example snippets from pod generator-3:
```
[2026-03-15T19:12:07Z] WARN Allocator: cudaMalloc failed; fallback to host allocation
[2026-03-15T19:12:07Z] INFO KVCache: entries=1_234_567, size=28.1GB
[2026-03-15T19:12:10Z] WARN InferenceLoop: step latency=120ms (kv_fetch), total=980ms
```
No full OOM kills (no dmesg oom kill lines), but nvidia-smi shows GPU memory pinned high and small spikes correlate with latency spikes.
Jordan: Can you paste `nvidia-smi` and `pmap` snapshot for the process? Also are these long-lived sessions keeping per-conversation KV caches forever?
Mia: nv-snapshot (abridged):
```
PID  12345 Name generator  GPU-Mem  45.2GB / 48GB
alloc spikes: 42GB -> 47GB under load
```
pmap snippet shows big anonymous regions (KV cache) growing over time. We confirmed a few heavy tenants had multi-hour conversations; kv_cache entries per-session were not evicting because TTL is off in this model's config.
SRE-Bot: Incident INC-2026-237 created: https://incidents/redwood/INC-2026-237 (latency/p99 regressions — suspected GPU memory pressure)
Sam: Two quick mitigations we can try now that are low-risk:
- Toggle per-request max_tokens down via runtime config for the affected model group (reduce prefix KV growth)
- Trigger rolling restart for generator shards to reclaim fragmented device memory
Commands:
```
# reduce tokens
curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://api.internal/config/models/redwood-medium -d '{"max_tokens":1024}'
# restart shard
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/generator-shard-3
```
Alex: Suggest also enabling KV eviction threshold so old conversation entries reclaim memory: set `kv_cache.eviction_threshold=0.8` and `kv_cache.eviction_policy=LRU` for the model group. That should prevent indefinite growth.
Elena: From runtime/allocator side, this smells like fragmentation + sustained allocations (large KV slabs). Two medium-term actions we should consider:
- Enable CUDA asynchronous allocator / memory pool so small frees don't fragment device memory (cudaMallocAsync + mempool). In our runtime config add `enable_cuda_mempool: true`.
- Tune host allocator (jemalloc) to reduce dirty pages: `MALLOC_CONF="narenas:4,lg_dirty_mult:8,decay_ms:1000"` for the worker containers.
Also add guard rails: per-tenant KV quotas and an eviction TTL default (e.g., 30m) so a runaway session can't blow memory.
Mia: Applied the token cap and started rollout at 19:18Z. After restart of two overloaded shards: p95 dropped to ~600ms, p99 ~1.1s. Still above baseline but much better. No customer 502s during test traffic.
Jordan: Good. Let's run a canary with mempool enabled on one shard to measure fragmentation improvements. Config to flip (example):
```
# runtime override for shard-5 (canary)
PATCH /runtime/overrides/shard-5
{"enable_cuda_mempool":true, "kv_cache":{"eviction_threshold":0.8, "max_entries":1000000}}
```
Monitor metrics: device_free_memory, curand_alloc_failures, allocator_fragmentation_ratio. Grafana panels to watch: gpu/mem_used, gpu/fragmentation, model/kv_entries_by_tenant.
Sam: I'll run the canary at 19:30Z and keep it under slack watch. If it looks stable for 30m we'll roll to remaining shards and make the allocator change a permanent runtime flag.
Elena: Long-term items (tickets):
- ENG-RUNTIME-462: Add support for cudaMallocAsync + mempool in our inference runtime and benchmark with typical KV workloads (owner: Elena)
- ENG-PLATFORM-311: Per-tenant KV quotas + TTL defaults + admin override knob (owner: Jordan)
- ENG-OBS-128: Add fragmentation and allocator-specific alarms to SLOs (owner: Alex)
Mia: Customer comms: I created ticket #CS-9621 and posted a short status to the customers affected (noting we're mitigating and expecting full rollback of latency in next 24h).  
Sam: Canary started. Early signal: shard-5 device fragmentation ratio dropped 18% within 5 minutes, p95 improved 20%. Rolling to rest of impacted shards in waves of 2.
SRE-Bot: Update INC-2026-237: mitigation applied — token cap + rolling restarts + canary mempool. Monitoring.
Mia: Closing loop — after full rollout p95 stabilized at ~420ms and p99 at ~750ms, within acceptable error budget. Follow-ups assigned as Elena/Jordan/Alex from earlier. I'll update CS ticket and mark incident resolved after postmortem.
Jordan: For the postmortem, include repro steps:
1) Start long-lived chat session and repeatedly append history until KV entries > 1M
2) Disable KV eviction TTL
3) Observe allocator fragmentation with `nvidia-smi` + runtime `allocator/fragmentation` metric
4) Reproduce latency spike and allocation fallbacks
Also include script to simulate workload (I'll add to repo infra/testbed)
Mia: Thanks all. Great coordinated response. :thumbsup:
